title: Hybrid token lineage reconciler with confidence scoring and graceful fallback allocation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reconciler service that merges streaming metering (real-time token events) with batch/retrospective consumption records and produces authoritative token-attribution entries for billing and console analytics. The service provides a per-event confidence score, preserves lineage for auditability, and applies deterministic fallback allocation when attribution signals are partial or missing. This addresses current gaps: late-arriving batch events causing under/over charging, opaque attribution when route/model metadata is missing, and brittle heuristics in the current billing joiner. The output must be idempotent, support replay, and emit lineage pointers usable by the Console and accounting pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler consumes kafka topic 'metering-stream' and S3 batch manifests and writes normalized attribution records to 'token-attribution-v2' topic
Attribution record includes: event_id, tenant_id, request_id, model_id, route_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp, confidence_score, lineage_refs (list of provenance ids)
Confidence scoring is computed using documented features (see technical_notes) and is reproducible across restarts
When model/route metadata is missing, fallback allocator applies deterministic rules (last_known_route -> proportional by model_weight -> tenant_unassigned) and tags records with fallback_reason
Service supports idempotent replays using stable dedupe keys and emits reconciliation metrics (matched, fallback, late-arrival, duplicate) to console dashboards
End-to-end integration test demonstrates correct reconciliation for a simulated late-arrival batch causing 3% adjustment and shows no double-charge with replay enabled
Backward compatibility: legacy billing consumer can switch to 'token-attribution-v2' in shadow mode for 2 weeks with <1% divergence before cutover
technical_notes: Input sources: streaming kafka 'metering-stream' (near real-time token delta records), batched S3 manifests from batch-aggregator, and 'route-metadata' service for enrichment

Core algorithm: join streaming deltas with batch consumption windows using session keys (tenant, request_id, session_start), compute feature vector: time_delta, presence_of_route, model_confidence, prior_prefix_cache_hit_rate, shard_assignment_score
Confidence scoring: logistic model (lightweight) with weights maintained in config store; score thresholds control autoswitch to fallback allocator
Dedup semantics: use event_fingerprint + source_namespace + monotonic_offset as idempotency key; maintain sliding dedupe window of 72h in RocksDB local store with periodic compaction
Failure modes: in case of downstream topic backpressure, buffer to spill S3 with ordered batch markers and resume without changing attribution ordering
Schema: Avro v2 with explicit field 'fallback_reason' and 'lineage_refs' (list of provenance ids). Must be forward/backward compatible
Operational constraints: single-tenant hotpaths may produce bursts; reconciler supports shard-level autoscaling and sticky partitioning by tenant hash
Security: PII-free payloads; tenant identifiers only. KMS-encrypted credentials for route-metadata service and Kafka clusters
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow): Deploy reconciler to staging and run in shadow mode against production traffic for 7 days, compare divergence metrics
Phase 2 (canary): Route 5% of production consumers to read from 'token-attribution-v2' topic for 48h, verify metrics and invoices for sample tenants
Phase 3 (gradual): Increase consumer traffic to 25% then 100% over 2 weeks, alert on divergence > 0.5%
Phase 4 (cutover): Promote v2 as canonical and deprecate legacy joiner; run one-week post-cut monitoring with rollback playbook ready
monitoring: Metrics: attribution_match_rate, fallback_rate, late_arrival_adjustment_rate, duplicate_event_rate, average_confidence_score
Dashboards: billing/reconciliation/ENG-850123 (link in links) shows time-series and tenant breakdown
Alerts: fallback_rate > 2% sustained for 30m, duplicate_event_rate spike > 0.1%
SLOs: 99.95% attribution stream write success; median processing latency < 200ms for streaming events
